title: Strategic Drift & Ansoff
welcome_lead: Spot strategic drift before the market moves on - then choose a growth route from Ansoff.
meta_desc: A-Level Business Strategy: strategic drift, Ansoff matrix four quadrants.
final_note: Watch the environment change, choose your Ansoff quadrant, and don't drift.

concepts.def: When a firm's strategy fails to keep pace with environmental change.
Selling more existing products to existing markets.
Selling existing products to new markets.
Selling new products to existing markets.
New products to new markets - the riskiest Ansoff quadrant.
Diversification risk is highest; market penetration is lowest.

walkthroughs.body_html: Johnson identifies incremental change, strategic drift, flux, then transformational change or death. Firms slip slowly out of step with customers - Kodak, Blockbuster and BlackBerry are textbook cases.

Ansoff plots products (existing vs new) against markets (existing vs new). Penetration grows share; market development opens new geographies; product development launches new lines; diversification does both at once.
The further you move from familiar products and markets, the higher the risk. Diversification can be related (synergies) or unrelated (conglomerate) - the latter rarely outperforms.

mcqs.q: Selling a new chocolate bar to existing supermarket customers is:

options: A firm changes strategy every year
Strategy fails to keep pace with environmental change
A firm exits all foreign markets
